title: Western Blot Protocol
author: Jeff Hodgin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.56hg9b6
materials: Make 4% stacking gel, pour stacking gel on top of the running gel and insert the comb (s), making sure there are no bubbles under the teeth of comb. Wipe off any stacking gel that ran over the side of the gel sandwich. Wait until gel is polymerized. While the gel polymerizes prepare samples and make 1x running buffer from 10 x stocks. Note: 4-12% pre cast gradient gel can be used to separate protein of all sizes very well and omits steps 1-6 (Novex Wedge well, 4-12% Tris-Glycine gel, 1.0mm x 15 well, Invitrogen, cat# XP04 125 BOX quantity 10/box).

steps.title: Prepare Casting Plates
steps.instruction: Clean and assemble the gel casting apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Wash plates and wipe the surface with ethanol, then dry.
Place the small glass plate on top of the big glass plate and fit into the casting stand with the small plate outside.
Close the casting frame door and fill the space between plates with H2O to check for leaks.
Mark a line 2cm from the top of the glass with a sharpie.
Pour off water and wipe dry with a Kim wipe, or use a thin strip of Whatman filter paper to dab remaining water from the bottom.

steps.title: Cast Separating Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the separating gel based on the target protein molecular weight.

substeps.instruction: Prepare separating gel in a 50ml conical tube; mix components by inverting the tube 6 times gently.
Pour gel using a 5ml or transfer pipette into the middle of the plates up to the 2cm mark.
Add 1ml of 2-propanol (or 1:10 water saturated n-Butanol, or absolute Ethanol) to level the gel and remove bubbles.
Wait approximately 40 minutes for polymerization.
Pour off 2-propanol and gently rinse the top of the gel with ddH2O.
Carefully blot off excess water with a thin strip of Whatman filter paper without touching the gel.

steps.title: Prepare Protein Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare and denature protein samples for loading.

substeps.instruction: Boil approximately 500 ml water in a 1000 ml Pyrex glass beaker on a hotplate.
Label screw top tubes for each sample.
Add 10-50 μg of each protein sample (or as needed) into labeled tubes.
Add 6x sample buffer at a 5:1 protein-to-buffer ratio (1/5 of protein volume) and adjust final volume with ddH2O.
Boil samples at 95ºC for 5 minutes (do not boil Bio Rad Precision Plus protein Dual color Standard markers).
Cool samples at room temperature and quick spin down.

steps.title: Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load samples and run the gel using a power supply.

substeps.instruction: Place gel inside the electrophoresis tank with the small plate inside, press down, and close doors.
Fill the inside of the chamber with 1x running buffer to about 1/2 way between the top of the small and large plate, then fill the outside and bottom of the apparatus.
Gently remove the comb and rinse each well with running buffer using a P-200 pipette to flush out broken gel pieces.
Load 5μl of protein marker, protein samples, and + & - controls.
Connect to power supply (red to red, black to black).
Run at 140 V for the stacking gel and 100 V for the separating gel.
Continue running for approximately 1-1/2 hour, or until the dye front runs off the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Prepare for Transfer
steps.instruction: Prepare the gel and nitrocellulose membrane for the transfer sandwich.

substeps.instruction: Separate glass plates, retrieve the gel, remove the stacking gel, and soak the gel in transfer buffer for 15 minutes.
Cut and label nitrocellulose membrane to the size of the gel (write only in the upper right corner with pencil).
Soak nitrocellulose membrane in distilled water for 5 minutes, then in transfer buffer for 10-15 minutes.
Soak two fiber pads and two medium-thick Whatman filter papers in transfer buffer.

steps.title: Assemble Transfer Sandwich
steps.instruction: Assemble the transfer sandwich in a gel holder cassette without air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Pour transfer buffer into a baking dish and place the gel holder cassette black side down.
Layer the sandwich in this order: 1 wet fiber pad (on black side), 1 Whatman filter paper, gel, nitrocellulose membrane, 1 Whatman filter paper, and 1 fiber pad.
Remove bubbles by rolling a 10ml pipette over the Whatman paper.
Squeeze out extra liquid and secure the sandwich with the plastic clip.

steps.title: Perform Protein Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to the membrane using an electrophoresis unit.

substeps.instruction: Place a small magnetic stir bar in the transferring tank.
Place the sandwich in the unit with the black part in the back.
Place electrodes on top (red to red, black to black).
Insert an ice pack into the apparatus and fill with 1X transfer buffer until the sandwich is covered.
Transfer at 0.25Amp constant current for 2-3 hours, or overnight in a cold room at 10-40mA.

steps.title: Verify Transfer and Wash
steps.instruction: Check transfer quality and clean the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Remove blot, briefly rinse in water, and stain with Ponceau S solution on a shaker until bands are visible.
Wash the blot quickly with 1x TBST.
Wrap the blot in saran wrap (no wrinkles) and make a photocopy.
Wash the membrane in 1X TBST 5-6 times for 5 minutes each wash on a shaker at room temperature.

steps.title: Block Membrane
steps.instruction: Block non-specific binding sites on the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Insert membrane into a seal meal bag.
Add 10ml of 5% non-fat milk in 1xTBST, remove bubbles, and seal with an electric sealer.
Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4ºC on a shaker.

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Dilute primary antibody (per manufacturer instructions) with 10ml of 5% non-fat milk in 1xTBST and vortex.
Remove blocking milk from the bag and add 10ml of diluted antibody.
Remove bubbles, seal the bag, and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature (turn membrane every 10-20 minutes) or overnight at 4ºC on a shaker.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with the secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Wash membrane 3 times for 5 minutes each with 1xTBST.
Dilute secondary antibody with 10ml of 5% non-fat milk in 1xTBST.
Place membrane in a new seal meal bag with 10ml of diluted secondary antibody, remove bubbles, and seal.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature on a shaker (turn membrane every 10-15 minutes).

steps.title: Final Washes
steps.instruction: Remove unbound antibodies from the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Quick rinse once with 1x TBST.
Wash 4-6 times for 5 minutes each with 1xTBST.
Wash in 1X TBS for 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Develop Membrane
steps.instruction: Apply ECL substrate and expose to X-ray film.

substeps.instruction: Place saran wrap over a clean glass plate and remove wrinkles.
Prepare ECL mix (1:1 mixture of solution 1 and 2; 4ml per gel) in a 15 mL conical tube by pipetting.
Add ECL mix over the membrane and let sit for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Dab the corner of the membrane on a paper towel to remove excess ECL.
Place membrane protein-side down on a second piece of saran wrap on a clean-dry glass plate.
Wrap the membrane with saran wrap (or plastic sheet protector), ensuring no wrinkles or bubbles on the protein side.
Place wrapped membrane protein-side up in a film cassette and secure with scotch tape.

steps.title: X-Ray Film Exposure
steps.instruction: Expose and develop the film in a dark room.

substeps.instruction: In a dark room under red safelight, wearing gloves, place film on top of the membrane.
Expose for 30 seconds initially; bend the upper right corner of the film for orientation.
Feed the film into the developing machine and press 'start'.
Adjust exposure time based on band intensity and background.
Place the developed film back over the membrane in the cassette (bent corner in upper right).
Trace protein marker bands from the membrane onto the film with a red marker.
